nodes.name: Composite minimization problem
nodes.statement: The composite minimization problem \begin{align} \min_{\xb\in \RR^d}~ f(\xb) + g(\xb) \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Minimize over $\RR^d$ the sum of a smooth loss $f$ and a nonsmooth regularizer $g$.

nodes.name: Finite-sum smooth loss
nodes.statement: Typically, the first term \begin{align} f(\xb) := \frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^n f_i(\xb) \end{align}

nodes.name: Lasso
nodes.statement: Lasso: least squares loss $f_i(\xb) = (y_i - \ab_i^\top \xb)^2$ and $\ell_1$ norm regularizer $g(\xb) = \|\xb\|_1$;

nodes.name: Logistic regression
nodes.statement: Logistic regression: logistic loss $f_i = \log(1+\exp(-y_i \ab_i^\top \xb_i))$;

nodes.name: Boosting
nodes.statement: Boosting: exponential loss $f_i(\xb) = \exp(-y_i \ab_i^\top\xb)$;

nodes.name: Support vector machines
nodes.statement: Support vector machines: hinge loss $f_i(\xb) =\max\{0, 1-y_i\ab_i^\top \xb\}$ and (squared) $\ell_2$ norm regularizer $g(\xb) = \|\xb\|_2^2$.

nodes.name: Asymptotic convergence of partially asynchronous gradient descent
nodes.statement: Asymptotic convergence of partially asynchronous gradient descent algorithm for solving unconstraint smooth optimizations is established in \cite{BT_parallel}, with its stochastic version being analyzed in \cite{BT_asy_gradient}.
nodes.statement_short: Prior work established asymptotic convergence of partially asynchronous gradient descent for smooth unconstrained problems.
conclusions: Asymptotic convergence of partially asynchronous gradient descent algorithm

nodes.name: B-step linear convergence of partially asynchronous gradient projection
nodes.statement: Asymptotic convergence of partially asynchronous gradient projection algorithm for solving smooth optimizations with convex constraint is established in \cite{BT_parallel}, and a ``B-step" linear convergence is further established in \cite{Tseng_linear_PAA} with an error bound condition.
nodes.statement_short: Prior work established asymptotic and, under an error bound, ``B-step'' linear convergence for partially asynchronous gradient projection.
assumptions: solving smooth optimizations with convex constraint
conclusions: a ``B-step" linear convergence is further established in \cite{Tseng_linear_PAA}

nodes.name: Subdifferential and critical point
nodes.statement: The Frech\'et subdifferential $\hat\partial h$ of $h$ at $\xb\in\dom h$ is the set of $\ub$ such that \begin{align} \liminf_{\zb\neq\xb, \zb\to\xb} \frac{h(\zb) - h(\xb) - \ub^\top(\zb-\xb)}{\|\zb-\xb\|} \geq 0, \end{align} while the (limiting) subdifferential $\partial h$ at $\xb\in\dom h$ is the ``closure'' of $\hat\partial h$: \begin{align} \{ \ub: \exists \xb^k \to \xb, h(\xb^k) \to h(\xb), \ub^k \in \hat{\partial} h(\xb^k), \ub^k \to \ub \}. \end{align} The critical points of $h$ are $\crit h := \{ \xb: \zero\in\partial h(\xb) \}$.
nodes.statement_short: Fréchet and limiting subdifferentials of a proper closed $h$, and its critical points $\crit h$.

nodes.name: Distance and projection
nodes.statement: The distance function \wrt a closed set $\Omega \subseteq \RR^d$ is defined as: \begin{align} \dist_{\Omega}(\xb) := \min_{\yb\in\Omega} \|\yb-\xb\|, \end{align} while the metric projection onto $\Omega$ is defined as: \begin{align} \proj{\Omega}(\xb) := \argmin_{\yb\in\Omega} \|\yb-\xb\|, \end{align} where $\|\cdot\|$ is the usual Euclidean norm.
nodes.statement_short: Distance from a point to a closed set $\Omega$ and the metric projection onto $\Omega$.
nodes.definiendum: The distance function \wrt a closed set $\Omega \subseteq \RR^d$

nodes.name: Proximal map
nodes.statement: The proximal map of a closed and proper function $h$ is (with parameter $\eta > 0$): \begin{align} \prox{h}(\xb) := \argmin_{\zb\in \RR^d} h(\zb) + \tfrac{1}{2\eta}\|\zb - \xb\|^2. \end{align} Occasionally, we will write $\prox[]{h}$ instead of $\prox[1]{h}$.
nodes.statement_short: Proximal map of $h$ with parameter $\eta>0$: the argmin of $h$ plus a quadratic proximity term.
nodes.definiendum: The proximal map of a closed and proper function $h$

nodes.name: Nonexpansiveness of the proximal map
nodes.statement: For convex functions, the proximal map is nonexpansive: \begin{align} \forall \xb, \forall \yb, ~ \|\prox{h}(\xb) - \prox{h}(\yb) \| \leq \|\xb - \yb\|, \end{align} while for nonconvex functions this may not hold everywhere.
nodes.statement_short: For convex $h$ the proximal map is $1$-Lipschitz; this can fail in the nonconvex case.

nodes.name: proximal gradient algorithm
nodes.statement: The proximal map is the key component of the proximal gradient algorithm \cite{FukushimaMine81} (\aka forward-backward splitting): \begin{align} \forall\,t = 0, 1, \ldots, \quad \xb(t+1) = \prox[\eta]{g}\big(\xb(t) - \eta \nabla f(\xb(t))\big), \end{align} where $\nabla f$ is the (sub)gradient of $f$, and $\eta$ is a suitable step size (that may change with $t$).
nodes.statement_short: Forward-backward splitting: a gradient step on $f$ followed by the proximal map of $g$.
input: $\eta$ is a suitable step size (that may change with $t$)

nodes.name: Convergence rate of the proximal gradient algorithm
nodes.statement: It is known that when $f$ is convex with $L$-Lipschitz continuous gradient and $0 < \eta < 2/L$, then $F_t := f(\xb(t))+g(\xb(t))$ converges to the minimum at the rate $O(1/t)$ and $\xb(t)$ converges to some minimizer $\xb^*$.
nodes.statement_short: For convex $f$ with $L$-Lipschitz gradient and $\eta<2/L$, function values converge at rate $O(1/t)$ and iterates to a minimizer.
conclusions: $F_t := f(\xb(t))+g(\xb(t))$ converges to the minimum at the rate $O(1/t)$

nodes.name: Convergence of proximal gradient under the KL inequality
nodes.statement: Recently, \cite{prox_alter_linear} proved that $\xb(t)$ converges to a critical point even for nonconvex $f$ and nonconvex and nonsmooth $g$ as long as together they satisfy a certain \KL inequality.
nodes.statement_short: Under a \KL inequality the proximal gradient iterates converge to a critical point even in the nonconvex nonsmooth case.
assumptions: nonconvex $f$ and nonconvex and nonsmooth $g$ as long as together they satisfy a certain \KL inequality

nodes.name: Bounded Below
nodes.statement: The function $F \!=\! f+g$ is bounded below.

nodes.statement_short: $\nabla f$ is $L$-Lipschitz.

nodes.name: Separable
nodes.statement: The function $g$ is closed and separable, \ie, $g(\xb) = \sum_{i=1}^{p} g_i(x_i)$.

nodes.name: Quadratic upper bound from smoothness
nodes.statement: It allows us to upper bound $f$ by its quadratic expansion at the current iterate---a standard step in the convergence proof of gradient type algorithms: \begin{align} \forall \xb, \forall \yb, ~f(\xb) \leq f(\yb) + \langle \xb - \yb, \nabla f(\yb) \rangle + \tfrac{L}{2} \|\xb - \yb\|^2. \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Descent-lemma quadratic upper bound on $f$ implied by $L$-Lipschitz gradient.

nodes.name: Separability of the proximal map
nodes.statement: The separable assumption on $g$ implies that \begin{align} \prox{g}(\xb) = \big( \prox{g_1}(x_1),~ \ldots~,~ \prox{g_p}(x_p) \big). \end{align}

nodes.name: Update on machine $i$
nodes.statement: Then, the update on machine $i$ is defined as: \begin{align} x_i \gets \prox{g_i}(x_i - \eta \nabla_i f(\xb^i)). \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Machine $i$ applies the proximal map of $g_i$ to a gradient step computed from its local full model.

nodes.name: m-PAPG
nodes.statement: Formally, the $t$-th iteration on machine $i$ can be written as: \begin{equation} \tag{\mspg} \left\{ \begin{aligned} \forall i,~ x_i(t+1) &= \begin{cases} x_i(t), & t \not\in T_i \\ \prox{g_i}(x_i(t) - \eta \nabla_i f(\xb^i(t))), & t \in T_i \end{cases} , \\ \mbox{(local) } \quad \xb^i(t) &= \big( x_1(\tau_1^i(t)),~ \ldots~,~ x_p(\tau_p^i(t)) \big), \\ \mbox{(global)}\quad \xb(t) &= \big( x_1(t),~ \ldots~,~ x_p(t) \big). \end{aligned} \right. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Model-parallel partially asynchronous proximal gradient: each machine updates its own block at its active clocks using a possibly stale local copy of the full model.
input: a global clock shared by all machines and denote $T_i$ as the set of active clocks when machine $i$ performs an update
$\tau_j^i(t) \leq t$ models the communication delay among machines

nodes.name: Block proximal-gradient update at active clocks
nodes.statement: \forall i,~ x_i(t+1) &= \begin{cases} x_i(t), & t \not\in T_i \\ \prox{g_i}(x_i(t) - \eta \nabla_i f(\xb^i(t))), & t \in T_i \end{cases}
nodes.statement_short: Machine $i$ updates $x_i$ by a proximal gradient step when $t\in T_i$, and leaves it unchanged otherwise.

nodes.name: Assemble the (stale) local full model
nodes.statement: \mbox{(local) } \quad \xb^i(t) &= \big( x_1(\tau_1^i(t)),~ \ldots~,~ x_p(\tau_p^i(t)) \big),
nodes.statement_short: Machine $i$ assembles its local full model from delayed components $x_j(\tau_j^i(t))$.

nodes.name: Global model for analysis
nodes.statement: \mbox{(global)}\quad \xb(t) &= \big( x_1(t),~ \ldots~,~ x_p(t) \big).
nodes.statement_short: Global model collects each machine's newest component.

nodes.name: Bounded Delay
nodes.statement: $\exists s \in \mathds{N}, ~\forall i, \forall j, \forall t, ~0 \leq t-\tau_j^i(t) \leq s$, $\tau_i^i(t) \equiv t$.
nodes.statement_short: Every component a machine reads is at most $s$ clocks stale, and each machine has its own component up to date.

nodes.name: Frequent Update
nodes.statement: $\exists s \in \mathds{N}, ~\forall i, \forall t, T_i \cap \{t, t+1, \cdots, t+s\} \ne \emptyset$.
nodes.statement_short: Every machine performs at least one update in any window of $s+1$ clocks.

nodes.name: Inconsistency bound between local and global models
nodes.statement: Let \Cref{assum:delay} hold, then the global model $\xb(t)$ and the local models $\{\xb^i(t)\}_{i=1}^p$ satisfy: \begin{align} \forall i=1,\cdots,p, ~~ \|\xb(t) - \xb^i(t)\| \leq \sum_{\dind = (t-s)_+}^{t-1} \| \xb(\dind+1) - \xb(\dind) \| \\ \|\xb^i(t+1) - \xb^i(t)\| \leq \sum_{\dind = (t-s)_+}^{t} \| \xb(\dind+1) - \xb(\dind) \|. \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: The local-global model gap is dominated by the sum of the last $s$ successive differences of the global sequence.

nodes.name: Proof of the inconsistency bound
nodes.statement: Indeed, by the definitions in \eqref{mspg_formulation}: \begin{align*} \|\xb(t) - \xb^i(t)\|^2 &= \sum_{j=1}^p \|x_j(t) - x_j(\tau_j^i(t)) \|^2 \\ &\leq \sum_{j=1}^p \left(\sum_{\dind = \tau_j^i(t)}^{t-1} \|x_j(\dind+1) - x_j(\dind) \|\right)^2 \\ &{\leq} \sum_{j=1}^p \left(\sum_{\dind = (t-s)_+}^{t-1} \|x_j(\dind+1) - x_j(\dind) \|\right)^2 \\ &=\sum_{j=1}^p \sum_{\dind = (t-s)_+}^{t-1} \sum_{\dind' = (t-s)_+}^{t-1} \|x_j(\dind+1) - x_j(\dind) \|\|x_j(\dind'+1) - x_j(\dind') \| \\ &=\sum_{\dind = (t-s)_+}^{t-1} \sum_{\dind' = (t-s)_+}^{t-1} \sum_{j=1}^p \|x_j(\dind+1) - x_j(\dind) \|\|x_j(\dind'+1) - x_j(\dind') \| \\ &{\leq}\sum_{\dind = (t-s)_+}^{t-1} \sum_{\dind' = (t-s)_+}^{t-1} \|\xb(\dind+1) - \xb(\dind) \|\|\xb(\dind'+1) - \xb(\dind') \| \\ &= \left(\sum_{\dind = (t-s)_+}^{t-1} \| \xb(\dind+1) - \xb(\dind) \|\right)^2, \end{align*} where the first inequality is due to the triangle inequality; the second inequality is due to \Cref{assum:delay}; and the last inequality follows from the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality. Similarly, \begin{align*} \|\xb^{i}(t) - \xb^{i}(t+1)\|^2 &= \sum_{j=1}^p \|x_j(\tau_{j}^i(t)) - x_j(\tau_{j}^i(t+1))\|^2 \\ &\leq \sum_{j=1}^p \left(\sum_{\dind = \tau_j^i(t)}^{\tau_j^i(t+1)-1} \|x_j(\dind+1) - x_j(\dind) \|\right)^2 \\ &\leq \sum_{j=1}^p \left(\sum_{\dind = (t-s)_+}^{t} \|x_j(\dind+1) - x_j(\dind) \|\right)^2, \end{align*} and the rest of the proof is completely similar to the previous case.
nodes.statement_short: Expand the squared norm coordinate-wise, then apply the triangle inequality, the bounded-delay assumption and Cauchy-Schwarz.

nodes.name: Bound the global-local gap
nodes.statement: Indeed, by the definitions in \eqref{mspg_formulation}: \begin{align*} \|\xb(t) - \xb^i(t)\|^2 &= \sum_{j=1}^p \|x_j(t) - x_j(\tau_j^i(t)) \|^2 \\ &\leq \sum_{j=1}^p \left(\sum_{\dind = \tau_j^i(t)}^{t-1} \|x_j(\dind+1) - x_j(\dind) \|\right)^2 \\ &{\leq} \sum_{j=1}^p \left(\sum_{\dind = (t-s)_+}^{t-1} \|x_j(\dind+1) - x_j(\dind) \|\right)^2 \\ &=\sum_{j=1}^p \sum_{\dind = (t-s)_+}^{t-1} \sum_{\dind' = (t-s)_+}^{t-1} \|x_j(\dind+1) - x_j(\dind) \|\|x_j(\dind'+1) - x_j(\dind') \| \\ &=\sum_{\dind = (t-s)_+}^{t-1} \sum_{\dind' = (t-s)_+}^{t-1} \sum_{j=1}^p \|x_j(\dind+1) - x_j(\dind) \|\|x_j(\dind'+1) - x_j(\dind') \| \\ &{\leq}\sum_{\dind = (t-s)_+}^{t-1} \sum_{\dind' = (t-s)_+}^{t-1} \|\xb(\dind+1) - \xb(\dind) \|\|\xb(\dind'+1) - \xb(\dind') \| \\ &= \left(\sum_{\dind = (t-s)_+}^{t-1} \| \xb(\dind+1) - \xb(\dind) \|\right)^2, \end{align*} where the first inequality is due to the triangle inequality; the second inequality is due to \Cref{assum:delay}; and the last inequality follows from the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality.
nodes.statement_short: Expand $\|\xb(t)-\xb^i(t)\|^2$ per coordinate and bound it by the squared sum of successive differences.

nodes.name: Bound the successive difference of the local model
nodes.statement: Similarly, \begin{align*} \|\xb^{i}(t) - \xb^{i}(t+1)\|^2 &= \sum_{j=1}^p \|x_j(\tau_{j}^i(t)) - x_j(\tau_{j}^i(t+1))\|^2 \\ &\leq \sum_{j=1}^p \left(\sum_{\dind = \tau_j^i(t)}^{\tau_j^i(t+1)-1} \|x_j(\dind+1) - x_j(\dind) \|\right)^2 \\ &\leq \sum_{j=1}^p \left(\sum_{\dind = (t-s)_+}^{t} \|x_j(\dind+1) - x_j(\dind) \|\right)^2, \end{align*} and the rest of the proof is completely similar to the previous case.
nodes.statement_short: Repeat the same estimate for $\|\xb^i(t+1)-\xb^i(t)\|$.

nodes.name: Square summability of the successive differences of m-PAPG
nodes.statement: Let \Cref{assum:bb,assum:smooth,assum:separable,assum:delay,assum:skip} hold. If the step size $\eta \in \left(0, \frac{1}{L(1+2\sqrt{p}s)}\right)$, then the sequence generated by \mspg is square summable, \ie \begin{align} \sum_{t=0}^{\infty} \|\xb(t+1) - \xb(t)\|^2 < \infty. \end{align} In particular, $\lim\limits_{t\to\infty} \|\xb(t+1) - \xb(t)\| = 0$ and $\lim\limits_{t\to\infty} \|\xb(t) - \xb^i(t)\| = 0$.
nodes.statement_short: For a small enough step size the m-PAPG iterates have square-summable successive differences, so both the increments and the local-global inconsistency vanish.
conclusions: the sequence generated by \mspg is square summable

nodes.name: Interpretation of the step size bound
nodes.statement: Our bound on the step size $\eta$ is natural: If $s = 0$, \ie, there is no asynchronism then we recover the standard step size rule $\eta < 1/L$ (we can increase $\eta$ by another factor of 2, had convexity on $g$ been assumed). As staleness $s$ increases, we need a smaller step size to ``damp'' the system to still ensure convergence. The factor $\sqrt{p}$ is another measurement of the degree of ``dependency'' among worker machines: Indeed, we can reduce $\sqrt{p}$ to $\sqrt{\sum_i L_i^2} / L$, where $L_i$ is the Lipschitz constant of $\nabla_i f$ (\cf \eqref{eq:Lip}).
nodes.statement_short: With no staleness the classical rule $\eta<1/L$ is recovered; larger $s$ or stronger inter-machine coupling forces a smaller step size.

nodes.name: Proof of square summability
nodes.statement:

nodes.statement_short: At inactive clocks reuse the last subgradient and control the extra gradient drift.

nodes.name: Combine the two cases
nodes.statement: Combining the two cases in \cref{sub_zero_1} and \cref{sub_zero_2} we have for all $t$: \begin{align} \| \ub(t+1) + \nabla f(\xb(t+1))\| \leq (\sqrt{p}/\eta + 2L) {\sum_{\dind = (t-2s)_+}^t} \| \xb(\dind+1) - \xb(\dind) \|, \end{align} where $\ub(t+1) = \big( u_1(t+1),~ \ldots~,~ u_p(t+1) \big) \in \partial g (\xb(t+1))$, and the factor $\sqrt{p} \geq 1$ is artificially introduced for the convenience of subsequent analysis. Therefore, by \cref{subdiff_bound} and \Cref{thm:limitcon} we deduce \begin{align} \lim_{t\to\infty} \dist_{\partial F(\xb(t+1))}(\zero) \leq \lim_{t\to\infty } \| \ub(t+1) + \nabla f(\xb(t+1))\| = 0. \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Merge both cases into one bound and conclude that $\dist_{\partial F(\xb(t+1))}(\zero)\to 0$.

nodes.name: Set up the function-value convergence
nodes.statement_short: Apply the proximal optimality inequality at $z=x_i^*$ to prepare an upper-semicontinuity estimate for the possibly discontinuous $g$.

nodes.name: Limsup bound over the active window
nodes.statement: Observe from \Cref{thm:limitcon} that \begin{align*} \lim_{m\to\infty} \max_{t \in [t_m-s, t_m + s]} \|\xb(t+1) - \xb^*\| = 0, \qquad \lim_{m\to\infty} \max_{t \in [t_m-s, t_m + s]} \|\xb^i(t+1) - \xb^*\| = 0. \end{align*} By \Cref{assum:skip}, $[t_m -s, t_m + s] \cap T_i \ne \emptyset$ for all $i$. Then using the Lipschitz continuity of $\nabla f$ we deduce from \cref{uniform} that \begin{align} \limsup_{m \to \infty} \max_{t\in[t_m-s, t_m+s] \cap T_i} g_i(x_i(t+1)) \leq g_i(x_i^*). \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Pass to the limit over the window $[t_m-s,t_m+s]\cap T_i$ to get $\limsup g_i \le g_i(x_i^*)$.

nodes.name: Extend the bound to the whole window
nodes.statement: Since each machine updates at least once during $[t_m-s, t_m]$, let $\hat t_m$ be the largest element of $[t_m-s, t_m] \cap T_i$. Also notice that each machine $i$ only updates at its active clocks $T_i$, it then follows that \begin{align*} \max_{t\in[t_m, t_m+s]} g_i(x_i(t+1)) = \max_{t\in[\hat t_m, t_m+s] \cap T_i} g_i(x_i(t+1)) \leq \max_{t\in[t_m -s, t_m+s] \cap T_i} g_i(x_i(t+1)), \end{align*} and hence by \eqref{eq:func_con} \begin{align} \limsup_{m \to \infty} \max_{t\in[t_m, t_m+s]} g_i(x_i(t+1)) \leq g_i(x_i^*). \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Use the frequent-update assumption to extend the limsup bound from active clocks to all clocks in $[t_m,t_m+s]$.

nodes.name: Conclude criticality
nodes.statement: To complete the proof, choose any $k_m\in [t_m, t_m+s]$. Since $\xb(t_m) \to \xb^*$, \Cref{thm:limitcon} implies that \begin{align} \xb(k_m) \to \xb^*. \end{align} From \cref{eq: usc} we know for all $i$, $\limsup\limits_{m\to\infty} g_i(x_i(k_m)) \leq g_i(x_i^*)$. On the other hand, it follows from the closedness of the function $g_i$ (\cf \Cref{assum:separable}) that $\liminf\limits_{m\to\infty} g_i(x_i(k_m)) \geq g_i(x_i^*)$, thus in fact $ \lim\limits_{m\to\infty} g_i(x_i(k_m)) = g_i(x_i^*) $. Since $f$ is continuous, we know \begin{align} \lim_{m\to \infty} F(\xb(k_m)) = \lim_{m\to \infty} f(\xb(k_m)) + \sum_i g_i(x_i(k_m)) = F(\xb^*). \end{align} Combining \cref{crit_1}, \cref{crit_2} and \cref{crit_3} we know from \Cref{def:sub} that $\xb^* \in \crit{F}$.
nodes.statement_short: Closedness of $g_i$ gives the matching liminf, hence $F(\xb(k_m))\to F(\xb^*)$ and $\xb^*\in\crit F$.

nodes.name: Comparison with the closest prior result
nodes.statement: \Cref{thm:limitcon_1} further justifies \mspg by showing that any limit point it produces is necessarily a critical point. Of course, for convex functions any critical point is a global minimizer. The closest result to \Cref{thm:limitcon} and \Cref{thm:limitcon_1} we are aware of is \cite[Proposition 7.5.3]{BT_parallel}, where essentially the same conclusion was reached but under the much more restrictive assumption that $g$ is an indicator function of a product \emph{convex} set. Thus, our result is new even when $g$ is a convex function such as the $\ell_1$ norm that is widely used to promote sparsity. Furthermore, we allow $g$ to be any closed separable function (convex or not), covering the many recent nonconvex regularization functions in machine learning and statistics (see \eg \cite{FanLi01,Mazumderetal11,Zhang10,ZhangZhang12}). We also note that the proof of \Cref{thm:limitcon_1} (for nonconvex $g$) involves significantly new ideas beyond those of \cite{BT_parallel}.
nodes.statement_short: The closest earlier result assumed $g$ to be the indicator of a convex product set; allowing any closed separable $g$ is new.

nodes.name: Existence of limit points
nodes.statement: We note that the existence of limit points can be guaranteed, for instance, if $\{\xb(t)\}$ is bounded or the sublevel set $\{\xb ~|~ F(\xb) \le \alpha \}$ is bounded for all $\alpha \in \RR$. However, we have yet to prove that the sequence $\{ \xb(t) \}$ generated by \mspg does converge to one of the critical points, and we fill this gap under two complementary sets of assumptions on the objective function in \Cref{sec: EB,sec: KL}, respectively.
nodes.statement_short: Limit points exist under boundedness of the iterates or of the sublevel sets; convergence of the whole sequence is deferred to the next two sections.

nodes.name: Convex
nodes.statement: The functions $f$ and $g$ in \eqref{compmin} are convex.

nodes.name: Error Bound
nodes.statement: For every $\alpha > 0$, there exist $\delta ,\kappa>0$ such that for all $\xb$ with $f(\xb) \leq \alpha$ and $\|\xb - \prox[]{g}(\xb - \nabla f(\xb))\| \leq \delta$, \begin{align} \dist_{\crit F}(\xb) \leq \kappa \|\xb - \prox[]{g}(\xb - \nabla f(\xb))\|, \end{align} where recall that $\crit F$ is the set of critical points of $F$.
nodes.statement_short: Near-stationary points at bounded function value are within $O(1)$ of the critical set, measured by the proximal gradient residual.

nodes.name: Prototypic convex function satisfying the error bound
nodes.statement: A prototypic convex function $F$ satisfying \eqref{eq:eb} is the following: \begin{align} F(\xb) = f(A\xb) + g(\xb), \end{align} where $f$ is strongly convex (\ie, $f-\tfrac{\mu}{2}\|\cdot\|^2$ is convex for some $\mu > 0$), $A$ is a linear map, and $g$ is either an indicator function of a convex set \cite{LuoTseng93} or the $\ell_p$ norm for $p\in [1,2]\cup\{\infty\}$ \cite{EB2015}. Many machine learning formulations such as Lasso and sparse logistic regression fit into this form.
nodes.statement_short: $F(\xb)=f(A\xb)+g(\xb)$ with strongly convex $f$ and $g$ an indicator or $\ell_p$ norm, e.g. Lasso.

nodes.name: Equivalence of the error bound with restricted strong convexity and quadratic growth
nodes.statement: In fact, for convex functions $F$ taking such form, the error bound condition in \cref{eq:eb} is recently shown to be equivalent to the following conditions \cite{DrusvyatskiyLewis16,Zhang2016}: \begin{align*} \text{Restricted strong convexity}: ~ &\inner{ \xb - \prox[]{g}(\xb)}{\xb - \proj{\crit F}(\xb)} \ge \mu \cdot \dist_{\crit F}^2(\xb), \\ \text{Quadratic growth}: ~ &F(\xb) - F^* \ge \mu \cdot \dist_{\crit F}^2(\xb), \end{align*} where $F^*$ is the minimum value of $F$ and $\mu>0$ is a constant.
nodes.statement_short: For such convex $F$ the error bound is equivalent to restricted strong convexity and to quadratic growth.
assumptions: for convex functions $F$ taking such form

nodes.name: Nonconvex instance of the error bound
nodes.statement: For instance, it holds for $f(\xb)= \tfrac{1}{2}\|\xb\|^2$ and any function $g$ that has a unique global minimizer at $0$ (such as the cardinality function $g(\xb) = \|\xb\|_0$).
nodes.statement_short: The error bound can hold without convexity, e.g. for a quadratic $f$ and the cardinality function $g$.

nodes.name: Progress quantities $A(t)$ and $B(t)$
nodes.statement: We define the following nonnegative quantities that measure the progress of \mspg: \begin{align} A(t) &:= F(\xb(t)) - F^*, ~ F^* :=\inf_{\xb} F(\xb), \\ B(t) &:= \sum_{k=(t-s-1)_+}^{t-1} \|\xb(k+1) - \xb(k)\|^2, \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: $A(t)$ is the objective gap and $B(t)$ the windowed sum of squared successive differences.

nodes.name: Recursive relations for the gap sequences
nodes.statement: Let \Cref{assum:bb,assum:smooth,assum:separable,assum:delay,assum:skip,assum:convex,assum:eb} hold. Then, we have \begin{align*} & A(t+s+1) \le A(t) - \tfrac{1}{2}(\tfrac{1}{\eta} - L - 2sL \sqrt{p}) B(t+s+1) + \tfrac{1}{2}sL\sqrt{p} B(t) \\ & 0 \le A(t+s+1) \le a_\eta B(t+s+1) + b B(t), \end{align*} where $a_\eta$ and $b$ are given in \eqref{eq:ab} below.
nodes.statement_short: Under the error bound, the objective gap after $s+1$ steps both decreases and is dominated by the windowed movement quantities.

nodes.statement_short: Nonexpansiveness of the proximal map turns each block movement into the proximal residual at $\zb$ up to $\eta L\|\zb-\xb^i(t_i)\|$.

nodes.name: Bound the staleness term
nodes.statement:
The last term $\|\zb - \xb^i(t_i)\|^2$ can be further bounded as follows:  egin{align} 
onumber \|\zb - \xb^i(t_i)\|^2 &= \sum_{j=1}^p \|x_j(t_j) - x_j (	au_j^i (t_i))\|^2 \ &= \sum_{j=1}^p \Big\|\sum_{k = \min\{ t_j, 	au_j^i(t_i) \} }^{\max\{ t_j, 	au_j^i(t_i) \}-1} x_j(k+1) - x_j(k) \Big\|^2 
onumber\ &\le \sum_{j=1}^p \Big[\sum_{k = \min\{ t_j, 	au_j^i(t_i) \} }^{\max\{ t_j, 	au_j^i(t_i) \}-1} \| x_j(k+1) - x_j(k) \| \Big]^2 
onumber\ &\overset{\mathrm{(i)}}{\le} \sum_{j=1}^p 2s \sum_{k= t-s}^{t+s-1} \| x_j(k+1) - x_j(k) \|^2 
onumber\ 
onumber &= 2s \sum_{k=t-s}^{t+s-1} \|\xb(k+1) - \xb(k)\|^2 \ & \leq 2s [B(t) + B(t+s+1)], \end{align} where (i) is due to the fact that $t_j \in [t, t+s]$ and $	au_j^i(t_i) \in [t-s, t+s]$. Combining \eqref{eq:proxb} and \eqref{eq:diff} we obtain  egin{align} \|\prox{g}(\zb - \eta 
abla f(\zb)) &- \zb\|^2 \leq 2 B(t+s+1) + 4ps\eta^2 L^2 [B(t) + B(t+s+1)]. \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Bound $\|\zb-\xb^i(t_i)\|^2$ by $2s[B(t)+B(t+s+1)]$ using the delay window.

nodes.name: Apply the error bound condition
nodes.statement:
Thanks to \Cref{thm:limitcon}, we know for $t$ sufficiently large, $\|\prox{g}(\zb \!-\! \eta 
abla f(\zb)) \!-\! \zb\| \leq \eta\delta$. Since the function $\eta \mapsto  rac{1}{\eta}\|\prox{g}(\zb \!-\! \eta 
abla f(\zb)) \!-\! \zb\|$ is monotonically decreasing \cite{Sra12}, we can apply the error bound condition in \Cref{assum:eb} for $\eta < 1$ and $t$ sufficiently large, and obtain  egin{align} \| ar\zb - \zb\|^2 \le \kappa \|\zb - \prox[]{g}(\zb - 
abla f(\zb))\|^2 \le \kappa \eta^{-2} \|\zb - \prox{g}(\zb - \eta
abla f(\zb))\|^2. \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Once the residual is small, the error bound converts it into a bound on $\|\bar\zb-\zb\|^2$.

nodes.name: Assemble the second recursion
nodes.statement: Finally, combining \eqref{eq:Fgap}, \eqref{eq:diff}, \eqref{eq:pb} and \eqref{eq:projdist} we arrive at: \begin{align} \nonumber F(\xb(t\!+\!s\!+\!1)) - F^* &= F(\zb^+) - F^* \\ \nonumber&\le (L\!+\!4)\|\bar\zb \!-\! \zb\|^2 + (L\!+\!4\!+\!\tfrac{4}{\eta^{2}}) B(t\!+\!s\!+\!1) + 4L^2\sum_{i=1}^{p} \|\xb^i (t_i) \!-\! \zb\|^2,\\ &\le a_\eta B(t+s+1) + b B(t), \end{align} where the coefficients are \begin{align} a_\eta &= L+4+8psL^2 + 4ps\kappa L^2(L+4) + \tfrac{2}{\eta^2}(2+4\kappa+\kappa L), \\ b &= 8psL^2+4ps\kappa L^2(L+4). \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Combine all estimates to obtain $A(t+s+1)\le a_\eta B(t+s+1)+bB(t)$ with explicit constants.

nodes.name: Improvement over the Tseng analysis
nodes.statement: \Cref{lemma: EB_2} improves the analysis of \cite{Tseng_linear_PAA} in three aspects: (1) it is shorter and simpler; (2) it allows any convex function $g$; and (3) the leading coefficient for $B(t)$ is reduced from $O(1/\eta)$ to $O(1)$.
nodes.statement_short: The lemma is shorter, allows any convex $g$, and improves the leading coefficient of $B(t)$ from $O(1/\eta)$ to $O(1)$.

nodes.name: Periodically linear convergence under the error bound
nodes.statement: Let \Cref{assum:bb,assum:smooth,assum:separable,assum:delay,assum:skip,assum:convex,assum:eb} hold. Then, there exists some $\eta_0 >0$ such that if $0<\eta<\eta_0$, then the sequences $\{A(t), B(t)\}$ generated by \mspg satisfy for all $r = 0, 1, 2, \cdots$ \begin{align} A(r (s+1)) \le C_1 (1-\gamma \eta)^{r}, ~B(r (s+1)) \le C_2 (1-\gamma \eta)^{r}, \end{align} where $C_1, C_2,\gamma<1/\eta$ are positive constants.
nodes.statement_short: The gap sequences decay geometrically in the number of $(s+1)$-blocks of iterations.
assumptions: there exists some $\eta_0 >0$ such that if $0<\eta<\eta_0$

nodes.name: The $(s+1)$-step time scale
nodes.statement: Hence, the gaps $A(t)$ and $B(t)$ that measure the progress of \mspg decrease by a constant factor $(1-\gamma \eta)$ for every $s+1$ steps, which makes intuitive sense since in the worst case each worker machine only performs one update in every $s+1$ steps. In other words, $(s+1)$ is the natural time scale for measuring progress here. Note that since $\|\xb(t+s+1) - \xb(t)\|^2 \leq (s+1) B(t+s+1)$, it follows easily that the global sequence $\xb(t)$ and consequently also the local sequences $\{ \xb^i(t) \}$ all converge to the same limit point in $\crit F$ at a $(s+1)$-periodically linear rate.
nodes.statement_short: $s+1$ is the natural time scale, since in the worst case a machine updates once per $s+1$ clocks; the iterates converge at an $(s+1)$-periodic linear rate.

nodes.name: KL property
nodes.statement: Let $\Omega\subset \mathrm{dom} h$ be a compact set on which the function $h$ is a constant. We say that $h$ satisfies the \KL property if there exist $\varepsilon, \lambda >0$ such that for all $\bar{\xb} \in \Omega$ and all $\xb\in \{\zb\in \RR^d : \dist_\Omega(\zb)<\varepsilon\}\cap [\zb: h(\bar{\xb}) < h(\zb) <h(\bar{\xb}) + \lambda]$, it holds that \begin{align} \varphi'(h(\xb) - h(\bar{\xb})) \cdot \dist_{\partial h(\xb)}(\zero) \ge 1, \end{align} where the function $\varphi: [0,\lambda) \to \RR_+, 0\mapsto 0$, is continuous, concave, and has continuous and positive derivative $\varphi'$ on $(0,\lambda)$.
nodes.statement_short: $h$ has the \KL property if a concave desingularizer $\varphi$ makes $\varphi'(h(\xb)-h(\bar\xb))\cdot\dist_{\partial h(\xb)}(\zero)\ge 1$ near a compact constancy set.
nodes.genus: a compact set on which the function $h$ is a constant
differentia: the function $\varphi: [0,\lambda) \to \RR_+, 0\mapsto 0$, is continuous, concave, and has continuous and positive derivative $\varphi'$ on $(0,\lambda)$

nodes.name: Sufficient decrease
nodes.statement: There exists $\alpha \!>\! 0$ such that for all large $t$, \begin{align} F(\xb(t+1)) \leq F(\xb(t)) - \alpha \|\xb(t+1) - \xb(t)\|^2. \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: The objective decreases by at least $\alpha\|\xb(t+1)-\xb(t)\|^2$ at every large $t$.

nodes.name: Finite Length
nodes.statement: Let \Cref{assum:bb,assum:smooth,assum:separable,assum:delay,assum:skip,assum:sd} hold for \mspg, and let $F$ satisfy the \KL property in \Cref{def:KL}. Then, with step size $\eta \in \left(0, \frac{1}{L(1+2\sqrt{p}s)}\right)$, every bounded sequence $\{\xb(t)\}$ generated by \mspg satisfies \begin{flalign} \sum_{t=0}^{\infty} \|\xb(t+1) - \xb(t)\| < \infty,\\ \forall i = 1, \ldots ,p, ~ \sum_{t=0}^{\infty} \|\xb^i(t+1) - \xb^i(t)\| < \infty. \end{flalign} Furthermore, $\{\xb(t)\}$ and $\{\xb^i(t)\}_{i=1}^p$ converge to the same critical point of $F$.
nodes.statement_short: Under the \KL property and sufficient decrease, the global and local trajectories have finite length and converge to one common critical point.
conclusions: Furthermore, $\{\xb(t)\}$ and $\{\xb^i(t)\}_{i=1}^p$ converge to the same critical point of $F$.

nodes.name: Proof of the finite length property
nodes.statement:
We first show that \cref{global_finite} implies \cref{local_finite}. Indeed, recall from \eqref{eq:local_diff}:  egin{align*} \|\xb^i(t+1) - \xb^i(t)\| &\leq \sum_{k=(t-s)_+}^{t} \|\xb(k+1) - \xb(k)\|. \end{align*} Therefore, summing for $t=0, 1, \cdots, n$ gives  egin{align*} \sum_{t=0}^n \|\xb^i(t+1) - \xb^i(t)\| &\leq \sum_{t=0}^n \sum_{k=(t-s)_+}^{t} \|\xb(k+1) - \xb(k)\| \ &\leq (2s+1) \sum_{t=0}^n \|\xb(t+1) - \xb(t)\|. \end{align*} The claim then follows by letting $n$ tend to infinity. By \Cref{thm:limitcon}, the limit points of $\{\xb(t)\}$ and $\{\xb^i(t)\}_{i=1}^p$ coincide and are critical points of $F$. Thus, the only thing left to prove is the finite length property in \cref{global_finite}. By \Cref{assum:sd} and \Cref{assum:bb}, the objective value $F(\xb(t))$ decreases to a finite limit $F^*$. Since $\{\xb(t)\}$ is assumed to be bounded, the set of its limit points $\Omega$ is nonempty and compact. Summing \cref{usc} over all $i$ and set $\zb \in \Omega$, we obtain \[ g(\xb(t+1)) \le g(\zb) -  rac{1}{2\eta} \|\xb(t+1) - \xb(t)\|^2 - \sum_{i=1}^{p}\inner{
abla_i f(\xb^i(t))}{\xb(t+1) - \xb(t)}. \] Note that $\xb(t+1) - \xb(t) 	o 0$. Also, since $\{\xb(t)\}$ is bounded and $\xb(t) - \xb^i(t)	o 0$ for all $i$, $\{\xb^i(t)\}_{i=1}^p$ are all bounded. we then take limsup on both sides and obtain that $\limsup_{t	o\infty} g(\xb(t+1)) \le g(\zb)$. Together with the closedness of $g$ we further obtain that $\lim_{t	o\infty} g(\xb(t+1)) = g(\zb)$. Note that $f$ is continuous, we thus conclude that $\lim_{t	o\infty} F(\xb(t+1)) = F(\zb)$ for all $\zb\in \Omega$. Note that $F(\xb(t)) \downarrow F^*$. Thus for all $\xb^* \in \Omega$, we have $F(\xb^*) \equiv F^*$. Now fix $\varepsilon > 0$. Since $\Omega$ is compact, for $t$ sufficiently large we have $\dist_{\Omega}(\xb(t)) \leq \varepsilon$. We now have all ingredients to apply the \KL inequality in \Cref{def:KL}: for all sufficiently large $t$,  egin{flalign} \varphi' ig(F(\xb(t)) - F^* ig) \cdot \dist_{\partial F(\xb(t))}(\zero) \ge 1. \end{flalign} Since $\varphi$ is concave, we obtain  egin{flalign} \Delta_{t,t+1} &:= \varphi ig(F(\xb(t)) - F^* ig) - \varphi ig(F(\xb(t+1)) - F^* ig) 
onumber\ &\ge \varphi' ig(F(\xb(t)) - F^* ig)  ig(F(\xb(t)) -F(\xb(t+1)) ig) 
onumber\ &\ovset{(i)}{\ge}  rac{\alpha \|\xb(t+1) - \xb(t) \|^2}{\dist_{\partial F(\xb(t))}(\zero)}, \end{flalign} where (i) follows from \Cref{assum:sd} and \cref{uKL}. It is clear that the function $\varphi$ (composed with $F$) serves as a Lyapunov function. Using the elementary inequality $2\sqrt{ab} \le a + b$ we obtain from \cref{Lyapunov} that for $t$ sufficiently large,  egin{flalign*} 2\|\xb(t+1) - \xb(t)\| \le 	frac{\delta}{\alpha} \Delta_{t,t+1} + 	frac{1}{\delta}\dist_{\partial F(\xb(t))}(\zero), \end{flalign*} where $\delta > 0$ will be specified later. Recalling the bound for $\partial F(\xb(t))$ in \cref{subdiff_bound}, and summing over $t$ from $m$ (sufficiently large) to $n$ gives:  egin{flalign*} 2\sum_{t=m}^{n}&\|\xb(t+1) - \xb(t)\| \le \sum_{t=m}^{n}  rac{\delta}{\alpha} \Delta_{t, t+1} + \sum_{t=m}^{n}  rac{1}{\delta} \dist_{\partial F(\xb(t))}(\zero) \ &\ovset{(i)}{\le}  rac{\delta}{\alpha} \varphi ig(F(\xb(m)) - F^* ig) + \sum_{t=m}^{n}  rac{\sqrt{p}/\eta + 2L}{\delta} \sum_{\dind = (t-2s)_+}^t \| \xb(\dind+1) - \xb(\dind) \| \ &\le  rac{\delta}{\alpha} \varphi ig(F(\xb(m)) - F^* ig) +  rac{(2s+1)(\sqrt{p}/\eta + 2L)}{\delta} \sum_{\dind=(m-2s)_+}^{m-1} \| \xb(\dind+1) - \xb(\dind) \| \ &\qquad\qquad \qquad\qquad +  rac{(2s+1)(\sqrt{p}/\eta + 2L)}{\delta} \sum_{t=m}^{n} \| \xb(t+1) - \xb(t) \|, \end{flalign*} where (i) is due to \cref{subdiff_bound}. Setting $\delta = (2s+1)(\sqrt{p}/\eta + 2L)$ and rearranging gives  egin{flalign*} \sum_{t=m}^{n}\|\xb(t+1) - \xb(t)\| &\le  rac{(2s+1)(\sqrt{p}/\eta + 2L)}{\alpha} \varphi ig(F(\xb(m)) - F^* ig) \ &\quad+ \sum_{\dind=(m-2s)_+}^{m-1} \| \xb(\dind+1) - \xb(\dind) \|. \end{flalign*} Since the right-hand side is finite, let $n$ tend to infinity completes the proof for \cref{global_finite}.
nodes.statement_short: Use $\varphi\circ F$ as a Lyapunov function: the \KL inequality plus sufficient decrease bound each increment, and summing telescopes to a finite total length.

nodes.name: Global finite length implies local finite length
nodes.statement: We first show that \cref{global_finite} implies \cref{local_finite}. Indeed, recall from \eqref{eq:local_diff}: \begin{align*} \|\xb^i(t+1) - \xb^i(t)\| &\leq \sum_{k=(t-s)_+}^{t} \|\xb(k+1) - \xb(k)\|. \end{align*} Therefore, summing for $t=0, 1, \cdots, n$ gives \begin{align*} \sum_{t=0}^n \|\xb^i(t+1) - \xb^i(t)\| &\leq \sum_{t=0}^n \sum_{k=(t-s)_+}^{t} \|\xb(k+1) - \xb(k)\| \\ &\leq (2s+1) \sum_{t=0}^n \|\xb(t+1) - \xb(t)\|. \end{align*} The claim then follows by letting $n$ tend to infinity.
nodes.statement_short: Sum the local-difference bound to get $\sum\|\xb^i(t+1)-\xb^i(t)\|\le(2s+1)\sum\|\xb(t+1)-\xb(t)\|$.

nodes.name: Objective values converge
nodes.statement: By \Cref{thm:limitcon}, the limit points of $\{\xb(t)\}$ and $\{\xb^i(t)\}_{i=1}^p$ coincide and are critical points of $F$. Thus, the only thing left to prove is the finite length property in \cref{global_finite}. By \Cref{assum:sd} and \Cref{assum:bb}, the objective value $F(\xb(t))$ decreases to a finite limit $F^*$.
nodes.statement_short: Sufficient decrease and boundedness below make $F(\xb(t))$ decrease to a finite limit.

nodes.name: Compare $g$ at the iterates with a limit point
nodes.statement: Since $\{\xb(t)\}$ is assumed to be bounded, the set of its limit points $\Omega$ is nonempty and compact. Summing \cref{usc} over all $i$ and set $\zb \in \Omega$, we obtain \[ g(\xb(t+1)) \le g(\zb) - \frac{1}{2\eta} \|\xb(t+1) - \xb(t)\|^2 - \sum_{i=1}^{p}\inner{\nabla_i f(\xb^i(t))}{\xb(t+1) - \xb(t)}. \]
nodes.statement_short: Sum the proximal optimality inequality at a limit point $\zb\in\Omega$.

nodes.name: $F$ is constant on the limit set
nodes.statement: Note that $\xb(t+1) - \xb(t) \to 0$. Also, since $\{\xb(t)\}$ is bounded and $\xb(t) - \xb^i(t)\to 0$ for all $i$, $\{\xb^i(t)\}_{i=1}^p$ are all bounded. we then take limsup on both sides and obtain that $\limsup_{t\to\infty} g(\xb(t+1)) \le g(\zb)$. Together with the closedness of $g$ we further obtain that $\lim_{t\to\infty} g(\xb(t+1)) = g(\zb)$. Note that $f$ is continuous, we thus conclude that $\lim_{t\to\infty} F(\xb(t+1)) = F(\zb)$ for all $\zb\in \Omega$. Note that $F(\xb(t)) \downarrow F^*$. Thus for all $\xb^* \in \Omega$, we have $F(\xb^*) \equiv F^*$.
nodes.statement_short: Upper semicontinuity plus closedness give $F(\xb(t+1))\to F(\zb)$, so $F\equiv F^*$ on $\Omega$.

nodes.name: Apply the KL inequality
nodes.statement: Now fix $\varepsilon > 0$. Since $\Omega$ is compact, for $t$ sufficiently large we have $\dist_{\Omega}(\xb(t)) \leq \varepsilon$. We now have all ingredients to apply the \KL inequality in \Cref{def:KL}: for all sufficiently large $t$, \begin{flalign} \varphi'\big(F(\xb(t)) - F^*\big) \cdot \dist_{\partial F(\xb(t))}(\zero) \ge 1. \end{flalign}
nodes.statement_short: Compactness of $\Omega$ puts the iterates in the \KL neighbourhood for large $t$.

nodes.name: Lyapunov decrease of $\varphi\circ F$
nodes.statement: Since $\varphi$ is concave, we obtain \begin{flalign} \Delta_{t,t+1} &:= \varphi\big(F(\xb(t)) - F^*\big) - \varphi\big(F(\xb(t+1)) - F^*\big) \nonumber\\ &\ge \varphi'\big(F(\xb(t)) - F^*\big) \big(F(\xb(t)) -F(\xb(t+1))\big) \nonumber\\ &\ovset{(i)}{\ge} \frac{\alpha \|\xb(t+1) - \xb(t) \|^2}{\dist_{\partial F(\xb(t))}(\zero)}, \end{flalign} where (i) follows from \Cref{assum:sd} and \cref{uKL}.
nodes.statement_short: Concavity of $\varphi$ turns the value decrease into a lower bound on $\Delta_{t,t+1}$.

nodes.name: Bound each increment by AM-GM
nodes.statement: It is clear that the function $\varphi$ (composed with $F$) serves as a Lyapunov function. Using the elementary inequality $2\sqrt{ab} \le a + b$ we obtain from \cref{Lyapunov} that for $t$ sufficiently large, \begin{flalign*} 2\|\xb(t+1) - \xb(t)\| \le \tfrac{\delta}{\alpha} \Delta_{t,t+1} + \tfrac{1}{\delta}\dist_{\partial F(\xb(t))}(\zero), \end{flalign*} where $\delta > 0$ will be specified later.
nodes.statement_short: Apply $2\sqrt{ab}\le a+b$ to bound $2\|\xb(t+1)-\xb(t)\|$ by the Lyapunov drop plus the subgradient distance.

nodes.name: Sum over $t$
nodes.statement: Recalling the bound for $\partial F(\xb(t))$ in \cref{subdiff_bound}, and summing over $t$ from $m$ (sufficiently large) to $n$ gives: \begin{flalign*} 2\sum_{t=m}^{n}&\|\xb(t+1) - \xb(t)\| \le \sum_{t=m}^{n} \frac{\delta}{\alpha} \Delta_{t, t+1} + \sum_{t=m}^{n} \frac{1}{\delta} \dist_{\partial F(\xb(t))}(\zero) \\ &\ovset{(i)}{\le} \frac{\delta}{\alpha} \varphi\big(F(\xb(m)) - F^*\big) + \sum_{t=m}^{n} \frac{\sqrt{p}/\eta + 2L}{\delta} \sum_{\dind = (t-2s)_+}^t \| \xb(\dind+1) - \xb(\dind) \| \\ &\le \frac{\delta}{\alpha} \varphi\big(F(\xb(m)) - F^*\big) + \frac{(2s+1)(\sqrt{p}/\eta + 2L)}{\delta} \sum_{\dind=(m-2s)_+}^{m-1} \| \xb(\dind+1) - \xb(\dind) \| \\ &\qquad\qquad \qquad\qquad + \frac{(2s+1)(\sqrt{p}/\eta + 2L)}{\delta} \sum_{t=m}^{n} \| \xb(t+1) - \xb(t) \|, \end{flalign*} where (i) is due to \cref{subdiff_bound}.
nodes.statement_short: Sum from $m$ to $n$ and insert the subdifferential bound.

nodes.name: Choose $\delta$ and conclude
nodes.statement: Setting $\delta = (2s+1)(\sqrt{p}/\eta + 2L)$ and rearranging gives \begin{flalign*} \sum_{t=m}^{n}\|\xb(t+1) - \xb(t)\| &\le \frac{(2s+1)(\sqrt{p}/\eta + 2L)}{\alpha} \varphi\big(F(\xb(m)) - F^*\big) \\ &\quad+ \sum_{\dind=(m-2s)_+}^{m-1} \| \xb(\dind+1) - \xb(\dind) \|. \end{flalign*} Since the right-hand side is finite, let $n$ tend to infinity completes the proof for \cref{global_finite}.
nodes.statement_short: Pick $\delta=(2s+1)(\sqrt{p}/\eta+2L)$, absorb the tail, and let $n\to\infty$.

nodes.name: Absolute versus square summability
nodes.statement: Compared with \eqref{sq_summable} in \Cref{thm:limitcon}, we now have the successive differences to be absolutely summable (instead of square summable). This is a significantly stronger result as it immediately implies that the whole sequence is Cauchy and hence convergent, whereas we cannot get the same conclusion from the square summable property in \Cref{thm:limitcon}. We note that local maxima are excluded from being the limit in \Cref{thm:finite}, due to \Cref{assum:sd}. Also, the boundedness assumption on the trajectory $\{\xb(t)\}$ is easy to satisfy, for instance, when $F$ has bounded sublevel sets. We refer to \cite[Remark 3.3]{KL_bound_sequence} for more conditions that imply the boundedness condition. Moreover, following similar arguments in \cite{KL_bound_sequence} we can also determine the local convergence rates of the sequences generated by \mspg.
nodes.statement_short: Absolute summability makes the sequence Cauchy, which square summability alone cannot give; local maxima are excluded and boundedness is easy to ensure.

nodes.name: All machines active at every clock
nodes.statement: $\forall i = 1, \cdots, p, \forall t, t \in T_i.$

nodes.name: Proximal Lipschitz
nodes.statement: We say a pair of functions $f$ and $g$ satisfy the proximal Lipschitz property on a sequence $\{\xb(t)\}$ if for all $\eta$ sufficiently small, there exists $L_\eta \in o(1)$, \ie $L_\eta \to 0$ as $\eta \to 0$, such that for all large $t$, \begin{align} \| \Delta_\eta(\xb(t)) - \Delta_\eta(\xb(t+1)) \| \le L_\eta \|\xb(t) - \xb(t+1)\|, \end{align} where\footnote{Should the proximal map be multi-valued, we contend with any single-valued selection.} $\Delta_\eta(\xb) \in \prox{g}(\xb - \eta\nabla f(\xb)) - \xb$.
nodes.statement_short: The proximal residual map $\Delta_\eta$ is Lipschitz along the sequence with a constant $L_\eta = o(1)$.

nodes.name: Proximal Lipschitz holds for smooth $f$ and $g$
nodes.statement: Suppose the functions $f$ and $g$ both have Lipschitz continuous gradient, then \Cref{assum:EL} holds for any sequence $\{\xb(t)\}$.
nodes.statement_short: If both $f$ and $g$ have Lipschitz gradients then the proximal Lipschitz assumption holds unconditionally.
assumptions: Suppose the functions $f$ and $g$ both have Lipschitz continuous gradient

nodes.statement:
Let us denote $L_f$ and $L_g$ as the Lipschitz constant of the gradient $
abla f$ and $
abla g$, respectively. Since $\Delta_\eta(\xb) \in \prox{g}(\xb - \eta 
abla f(\xb)) - \xb$, using the optimality condition for the proximal map, see for instance \cite[Proposition 7(iii)]{YuZMX15}, we have $$ \xb + \Delta_\eta(\xb) + \eta 
abla g ig(\xb + \Delta_\eta(\xb) ig) = \xb - \eta 
abla f(\xb), $$ and similarly $$ \zb + \Delta_\eta(\zb) + \eta 
abla g ig(\zb + \Delta_\eta(\zb) ig) = \zb - \eta 
abla f(\zb). $$ Subtracting one inequality from another, we obtain  egin{align*} \|\Delta_\eta(\xb) - \Delta_\eta(\zb)\| &= \|\eta

Clearly, when $\eta$ is mall, the leading coefficient $	frac{\eta(L_f+L_g)}{1-\eta L_g} \in \mathcal{O}(\eta) \subseteq o(1)$, and our proof is complete.

nodes.name: Write the optimality conditions at two points
nodes.statement:
Let us denote $L_f$ and $L_g$ as the Lipschitz constant of the gradient $
abla f$ and $
abla g$, respectively. Since $\Delta_\eta(\xb) \in \prox{g}(\xb - \eta 
abla f(\xb)) - \xb$, using the optimality condition for the proximal map, see for instance \cite[Proposition 7(iii)]{YuZMX15}, we have $$ \xb + \Delta_\eta(\xb) + \eta 
abla g ig(\xb + \Delta_\eta(\xb) ig) = \xb - \eta 
abla f(\xb), $$ and similarly $$ \zb + \Delta_\eta(\zb) + \eta 
abla g ig(\zb + \Delta_\eta(\zb) ig) = \zb - \eta 
abla f(\zb). $$
nodes.statement_short: State the proximal optimality identity at $\xb$ and at $\zb$.

nodes.name: Subtract and use Lipschitz gradients
nodes.statement:

nodes.name: Finite length under the proximal Lipschitz property
nodes.statement: Let \Cref{assum:bb,assum:smooth,assum:separable,assum:delay,assum:always} hold for \mspg, and let $F$ satisfy the \KL property in \Cref{def:KL}.
